name: Grain Growth
desc: A Potts-model polycrystal annealing under the microscope: grain boundaries creep toward their centre of curvature, big grains devour their small neighbours and triple junctions pull to 120 degrees, while waves of recrystallisation seed fresh strain-free nuclei that sweep through and consume the coarsened structure so it never settles; shown as a petrographic thin section under slowly crossed polars, an EBSD orientation map, a greyscale etched-and-polished metallographic section, or a bare boundary network in blueprint.

energy.doc: contrast and colour gain of the section (higher = brighter, harder boundaries)

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the section - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: Monte-Carlo sweeps/frame = how fast boundaries migrate, and the stage rotation rate

density.doc: recrystallisation nucleation rate - grain count at steady state (0 = a few huge grains, 1 = a fine dense mosaic)

temp.doc: annealing temperature - boundary roughness and thermal wander (high = ragged, fuzzy seams)

grain.doc: band contrast, polishing scratches and film tooth

hue.doc: base hue of the orientation / interference colour wheel

x.doc: pan across the section when magnified

y.doc: pan down the section when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: crossed-polar thin section with interference colour / EBSD false-colour orientation map / greyscale etched metallographic section / blueprint boundary network
